name: walkthrough
title: Python for Language Work
description: This tour walks through Python data structures, file I/O, classes, generators, regex capture groups, and other tools used for building language processors.

steps.description: A list of token rule pairs, a dictionary of ages, and demonstrations of list append, dict get with default, membership test, and iteration over items.
Output shows: 36, None, 0, True, then the two key-value pairs
Move to nested dictionaries and safe access with chained get.
A nested dictionary representing a state transition table, showing direct access, chained access, and safe access with default empty dict.
Output shows the nested dict, green, red, None
Move to sets and frozensets.
A set created empty, items added with add and update, membership tests, union, intersection, and a frozenset used as a dictionary key.

steps.question: What is the intersection of {"a", "b"} and {"b", "c"}?

steps.description: Output shows union ['a', 'b', 'c'], intersection ['b'], and the frozenset dict lookup
Move to strings and f-strings.
F-strings with !r for repr, split on newline and comma, strip whitespace, iteration over characters, and string length with indexing and slicing.

steps.question: What does f"read {symbol!r}" print when symbol is "a"?

steps.description: Output shows formatted strings, split results, strip, character loop, and length/index/slice
Move to files, JSON, and command line arguments.
A program that writes JSON to a file, reads it back, prints values, reads command-line arguments, and handles a missing file with try/except.

steps.question: What does the program print for sys.argv[1:] when run with arguments a b?

steps.description: Output shows: demo 2, empty list for argv, then no such file
Move to functions, modules, and __main__ guard.
A double function, a main function that prints double(21), and the if __name__ == "__main__" guard that runs main only when the file is executed directly.

steps.question: What does the program print when run directly?

steps.description: Output shows: 42
Move to a Counter class.
A Counter class with __init__ setting a start value, a bump method that increments and returns the count, and a demo creating Counter(5) and calling bump twice.

steps.question: What does c.bump() return the second time it is called?

steps.description: Output shows: 6 7 7
Move to a Point dataclass.
A Point dataclass with x required and y defaulting to 0, creating Point(3) and printing the repr, x value, and equality with Point(3, 0).

steps.question: What is the default value of y when only x is provided?

steps.description: Output shows: Point(x=3, y=0) 3 True
Move to a custom ConfigError exception.
A ConfigError exception subclass that stores a line number and formats the message, raised and caught in a try/except block printing the error and line.

steps.question: What does the except block print for the raised ConfigError?

steps.description: Output shows: line 7: bad value | 7
Move to lexer tools: SPEC list, compiled regex match vs search, generators, and Token dataclass.

A token specification list, compiled regex showing match at position vs search skipping ahead, a generator yielding values with StopIteration, and a Token dataclass with type, value, line, col fields.

steps.question: What does INT.match(source, 0) return for source "x = 42"?

steps.description: Output shows: None, then match at position 4 with group 42, start 4, end 6, search finds 42, generator yields 0 1, StopIteration, list [0,1,2], Token repr, equality True
Move to generators and yield.
A three_letters generator that prints started, yields a, prints resumed, yields b, prints resumed, and demonstrates next calls and StopIteration when exhausted.

steps.question: What does the first next(gen) print before yielding "a"?

steps.description: Output shows: nothing has run yet, started, a, resumed after a, b, resumed after b, StopIteration
Move to a words generator that skips spaces and yields words with positions.
A words generator that yields (word, start) for each run of letters, skipping spaces, raising ValueError on unexpected characters, and demonstrating next calls and a for loop.

steps.question: What does the second next(gen) return for input "let x ?"?

steps.description: Output shows: ('let', 0), ('x', 4), the caller could stop message, ValueError for ?, then for loop prints let 0 and x 4
Move to capture groups and group references in regex.

A comprehensive demo of regex capture groups: numbered groups, alternation inside groups, non-capturing groups, group references in re.sub with \1 \2 \3 and \g<n>, named groups with ?P<name> and \g<name>, word boundaries, replacing within a group, and a lambda function in re.sub.

steps.question: What does re.sub(ISO, r"\3.\2.\1", text) produce for the first date 2026-09-18?

steps.description: Output shows group captures, alternation difference, fullmatch results, non-capturing group shifts numbers, substitution to DD.MM.YYYY, raw string vs not raw, \g<n> form, named group substitution, m.groupdict, word boundary effect, token redaction, year change, and lambda substitution
